**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

configure_mappers() shouldn't have anything to do with this.  

if you're able to call expire_instance() and it works, then yes, you're done.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

no not at all.  configure_mappers() can only affect a mapper once, and only involves relationships.   if you were to add a new relationship to an already configured mapper, it fully configures that relationship on the fly (e.g. resolves what it points to).

**Dmytro Starosud ([@dima-starosud](https://github.com/dima-starosud)) wrote:**

@zzzeek

Did I understood correctly (also taking this ticket into account) that currently there is no way to see just added e.g. `hybrid_property` in `all_orm_descriptors` (off course if `all_orm_descriptors` was called already before)?

If I am creating child model inheriting from already configured base, will it be configured immediately?

Sorry for so many questions.

Thanks in advance!

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

it is a memoized collection.   nothing is in it until you call upon it, then it populates and it's done.

things really might be easier if you just get the collection more manually.  it's really simple, just walk through every key in the class:


```
from sqlalchemy.orm import interfaces

def all_orm_descriptors(my_class):
    for key in dir(my_class):
        attr = getattr(my_class, key)
        if isinstance(attr, interfaces.InspectionAttr):
           yield attr

```

Thanks in advance!

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Expire memoizations on setattr/delattr, check in delattr

Fixed bug where declarative would not update the state of the
:class:`.Mapper` as far as what attributes were present, when additional
attributes were added or removed after the mapper attribute collections had
already been called and memoized.  Addtionally, a ``NotImplementedError``
is now raised if a fully mapped attribute (e.g. column, relationship, etc.)
is deleted from a class that is currently mapped, since the mapper will not
function correctly if the attribute has been removed.

Change-Id: Idaca8e0237b31aa1d6564d94c3a179d7dc6b5df9
Fixes: #4133
